stories.why_ar: أشهر حكاية عن البطء. وهي ليست عن السرعة، بل عن التوقّف.
lines: A hare laughed at a tortoise every day.
"You are so slow," he said. "You will never win anything."
The tortoise did not shout back. She said, "Let us race."
All the animals came to watch.
The hare ran very fast and soon he could not see the tortoise behind him.
"I have hours," he thought. "I will sleep under this tree."
The tortoise did not stop. She walked, and walked, and walked.
She passed the sleeping hare without a sound.
When the hare woke up, he ran as fast as he could.
But the tortoise was already at the line, and the animals were cheering.
stories.moral_en: Slow and steady wins the race.
stories.moral_ar: لا يسبق السريعُ الذي ينام، وإنّما يسبق البطيءُ الذي لا يقف.

stories.why_ar: لا أحد أصغر من أن ينفعك يوماً.
lines: A lion was sleeping when a small mouse ran over his face.
The lion woke up and caught the mouse in his big paw.
"Please let me go," said the mouse. "One day I will help you."
The lion laughed. "You? Help me?"
But he was in a good mood, so he opened his paw.
Some weeks later, hunters caught the lion in a strong net.
He roared and pulled, but he could not get out.
The little mouse heard him and came running.
She cut the ropes with her sharp teeth, one by one, all night.
In the morning the lion was free.
stories.moral_en: No act of kindness is ever wasted.
stories.moral_ar: ما ضاع معروفٌ قطّ، ولو صنعتَه إلى من تظنّه لا يقدر.

stories.why_ar: حين لا تستطيع الوصول إلى ما تريد، غيّر الوضع لا نفسك.
lines: It was a very hot summer and the rivers were dry.
A thirsty crow found a tall pitcher with a little water in it.
He put his head inside, but his beak could not reach the water.
He pushed the pitcher. It did not fall.
He tried again. It still did not fall.
Then the crow saw small stones on the ground.
He picked up one stone and dropped it into the pitcher.
Then another. Then another.
Slowly, slowly, the water came up.
At last the crow drank, and flew away.
stories.moral_en: Little by little does the trick.
stories.moral_ar: القليل المتكرّر يبلغ بك ما لا تبلغه القوّة مرّةً واحدة.

stories.why_ar: ما تفعله في الصيف هو ما تأكله في الشتاء.
lines: All summer, a grasshopper sang in the warm grass.
Near him, the ants carried food to their home, again and again.
"Why do you work on such a beautiful day?" he asked.
"We are getting ready for the winter," said an ant.
The grasshopper laughed and went on singing.
Then the cold came, and the fields were empty.
The grasshopper had nothing to eat.
He went to the ants and asked for food.
"What did you do all summer?" they asked.
"I sang," he said. And he was quiet for a long time.
stories.moral_en: There is a time for work and a time for play.
stories.moral_ar: الشتاء لا يسأل عن أعذارك، بل عمّا خزّنته.

stories.why_ar: أغلى ما تملكه أن يُصدَّق كلامك.
lines: A boy watched the village sheep on the hill every day.
He was bored, so one day he shouted, "Wolf! Wolf!"
The village men ran up the hill with sticks.
There was no wolf. The boy laughed at them.
A week later he did it again, and again they came running.
Again there was no wolf, and this time nobody laughed.
Then, one evening, a real wolf came out of the trees.
The boy shouted, "Wolf! Wolf!" with all his voice.
The men heard him in the village, and did not move.
Nobody believes a boy who plays with the truth.
stories.moral_en: A liar is not believed even when he speaks the truth.
stories.moral_ar: من كذب مرّتين لم يُصدَّق في الثالثة ولو صدق.

stories.title_en: The North Wind and the Sun
stories.why_ar: الرفق يبلغ ما لا تبلغه القوّة.
lines: The north wind and the sun argued about who was stronger.
A traveller was walking below them in a warm coat.
"The one who takes off his coat is the stronger," they agreed.
The wind blew hard and cold.
The traveller held his coat tightly and pulled it closer.
The wind blew harder, and the man held on harder.
At last the wind stopped, tired.
Then the sun came out, quiet and warm.
The traveller felt the heat and opened his coat.
A minute later, he took it off and sat under a tree.
stories.moral_ar: ما شُدّ بالعنف يُشَدّ عليه، وما لُيّن باللين انفتح.

stories.why_ar: واحدكم وحده يُكسَر، ومجتمعين لا تُكسرون.
lines: An old farmer had four sons who argued every day.
One morning he asked them to bring him a bundle of sticks.
He gave the whole bundle to the oldest son.
"Break it," he said. The son tried, and could not.
Each son tried. The bundle did not break.
Then the farmer opened the bundle and gave each son one stick.
"Now break it."
Every stick broke easily.
"You are the sticks," said the father.
"Alone, anyone can break you. Together, nobody can."
stories.moral_en: Together we stand; apart we fall.

stories.title_en: The Goose That Laid the Golden Eggs
stories.why_ar: من استعجل الشيء قبل أوانه عوقب بحرمانه.
lines: A poor farmer found a golden egg under his goose.
He took it to the market and came home rich.
The next morning there was another golden egg.
And the next. And the next.
The farmer bought land, and then a bigger house.
But one egg a day was slow for him now.
"There must be gold inside her," he thought.
So he killed the goose and opened her.
There was no gold inside — only a bird like any other.
And there were no more eggs after that day.
stories.moral_ar: الجشع يقتل البطّة التي تُطعمك كل يوم.

lines: A great oak tree grew beside a river.
Below it, thin reeds moved with every small wind.
"You are weak," said the oak. "Any breeze moves you."
"We bend," said the reeds. "We do not fight the wind."
One night a storm came down the valley.
The oak stood straight and would not move.
The reeds lay down flat under the wind.
In the morning, the reeds stood up again, wet but whole.
The great oak was on the ground, its roots in the air.
The river carried its branches away.
stories.moral_en: Better to bend than to break.
stories.moral_ar: أن تلين فتبقى، خيرٌ من أن تصلُب فتنكسر.

stories.why_ar: من طلب ما ليس له أضاع ما في يده.
lines: A dog found a good piece of meat and carried it home.
On the way he crossed a narrow bridge over a river.
He looked down and saw another dog in the water.
That dog was carrying meat too — and it looked bigger.
He wanted that piece as well.
So he opened his mouth to bark at the other dog.
His own meat fell into the river.
The other dog disappeared at the same moment.
The water took the meat away.
The dog walked home slowly, with nothing.
stories.moral_en: Grasp at the shadow and lose the substance.
stories.moral_ar: من فتح فمه للظلّ سقط منه الأصل.
